title: observability(api): add request IDs, trace propagation, structured logs and per-endpoint metric tags; update openai-compat streaming
author: Ava Patel
description: Summary: Adds end-to-end observability improvements for the API surface: consistent request IDs, automatic trace/context propagation, structured JSON logs for inbound requests/responses/errors, and per-endpoint metric tags to enable fine-grained cost/latency dashboards. Also includes compatibility-layer fixes for OpenAI-style streaming and function/tool-calling so traces and request IDs surface end-to-end. Motivation: customers and SRE have requested reliable traceability across the hosted/dedicated/private deployment modes (ENG-4123). Current gaps: no stable request ID header, traces sometimes get lost across the gateway->runtime boundary, logs are free-form and not easily queryable by request_id or endpoint, and metrics are aggregated without a tag for route/model which makes per-endpoint cost/latency analysis difficult. Design highlights: 1) Request ID: introduce X-Redwood-Request-Id header generation in the API gateway when absent and transparently accept upstream request IDs. Request IDs are attached to all logs/metrics/traces. 2) Trace propagation: wire OpenTelemetry-compatible context across service RPCs (gateway->router->runtime) using W3C traceparent and baggage; extract and inject in the OpenAI compatibility layer too. 3) Structured logs: replace key request logs with JSON logger entries (timestamp, level, request_id, trace_id, route, model, customer_id*, latency_ms, http_status, error_code) and keep legacy text log for compatibility. 4) Per-endpoint metric tags: augment key counters/histograms with route and model tags (route: /v1/chat/completions, /v1/embeddings, etc.), and surface these tags to Prometheus and our metrik ingestion to support per-route dashboards. 5) OpenAI compatibility: streaming changes to ensure each chunk in Server-Sent Events includes request_id metadata and that function-calling events carry trace context so downstream tool runners can correlate. Rollout plan: feature-flagged on gateway and runtime, gradual ramp in 4 stages: dev, canary (5% traffic), staged (50%), global. Backwards compatibility: header acceptance is additive; when request IDs are absent we generate one. Trace changes are additive and respect existing traceparent headers. Telemetry knobs are behind switches to avoid overhead for critical low-latency customers. Tests and verification: unit tests for header propagation and logger formatting; integration e2e tests for trace continuity across gateway->runtime with simulated streaming; added new CI e2e that validates per-endpoint metric labels are present; manual verification on canary with flamegraphs and latency histograms. Observability artifacts: dashboards added for per-route latency and cost, and a log query cookbook in the docs. Security and privacy: no customer PII is added to logs; customer_id is a hashed id in telemetry. Related work: references ENG-4123, ENG-4098 and SUP-321. See docs update redwood-docs/content/api/observability.md. Checklist: [x] request id header generation/acceptance [x] trace extract/inject [x] structured logger and log schema [x] metric tags + Prometheus exposure [x] OpenAI-compat streaming propagation [x] unit + integration tests [x] docs and dashboards [x] feature flags and rollout notes

feat: wire otel context in rpc layer and add extract/inject helpers
chore: add structured logger and update request handlers to use json logger
feat: tag metrics with route/model and expose labels to prometheus
fix: openai-compat streaming include request_id and trace headers in sse chunks
docs: add api observability doc and dashboard json

review_conversation: Liam Chen: Please ensure the request ID is canonicalized (lowercase) and that we never log the raw Authorization header. Also add a unit test for header precedence (client-supplied vs generated).
Ava Patel: Added canonicalization and a sanitizer that strips Authorization and Cookie from structured logs. Unit test added in logging_test.go.
Sofia Martinez: The Prometheus exposition needs to keep cardinality low; can we limit model tag to known-buckets for embeddings vs general text models?
Ava Patel: Implemented model grouping via metric label sanitization: model_group with values {chat,embed,rerank,other} to avoid high-cardinality. Kept full model id in internal tracing tags only.
Ethan Brooks: Integration test flakes on CI for streaming e2e (timing). Suggest adding deterministic timing and retry on transient read.
Ava Patel: Adjusted test to use a deterministic test harness and added a single retry for transient network flakiness. CI passes locally.
Sofia Martinez: Approved after model_group change and docs update.
Liam Chen: Approved. Merging once CI green and smoke run on canary is done.
release_notes: Add stable request ID header (X-Redwood-Request-Id), automatic W3C traceparent propagation, structured JSON logs with request_id/trace_id/route/model_group, and per-endpoint metric tags. OpenAI compatibility layer streaming now includes request_id and trace metadata for tool/function-calling correlation. Feature-flagged rollout under observability.feature_toggle. No API-breaking changes.
notes: Follow-up work: instrument private installer paths and on-prem sidecars (ENG-4201), and add customer-configurable sampling for traces (ENG-4210). Canaries scheduled 2026-02-28.
